angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 269,932 km at 137.46 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.2750 +/- 0.0420 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 137.46 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.388 +/- 0.016 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-124 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract): 269,932 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.39 +/- 0.013 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-124 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3570 +/- 63 K from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-124 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-124 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-124.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.851, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-124 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.023 dex, from Livingston et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..102L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-124 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.65919, from Pope et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.461.3399P/abstract)
